issues.description: install.sh version guard still uses -lt 7 while the error message advertises >= 3.10
issues.detail: The user-facing message says '>= 3.10 and < 3.13' but the numeric check remains `[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ]`. Python 3.7-3.9 silently pass the guard and then fail later in confusing ways. Tighten the bound to match the documented minimum so the predicate and the message agree.

issues.description: Stale '< 3.10 compatibility' comments and the default_raise workaround remain after 3.9 was dropped
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py still carries comments stating default_raise exists 'for < 3.10 compatibility' and the helper itself survives. With kw_only native, fields using `field(default_factory=default_raise)` can be declared as plain required kw-only fields. Delete the helper and the misleading comments in this same patch.

issues.description: PR mixes three unrelated changes that should be split for clean bisect
issues.detail: Dropping 3.9 from CI/install, collapsing sys.version_info branches around kw_only dataclasses, and the drive-by switch from `zip(x, x[1:])` to `itertools.pairwise` are three independent patches. Bundling them makes reverts non-surgical when one regresses. Split into separate commits.

issues.description: dnf search lines added to install-scripts workflow are debugging noise
issues.detail: The Amazon Linux and Rocky prep blocks run `dnf search python3.12` between update and install. The output gates nothing and only spams logs while slowing CI. Drop the search lines or replace with an explicit version-pinned install step.

issues.description: Inlined @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) loses the named intent of kw_only_dataclass
issues.detail: The PR removed the kw_only_dataclass helper and replaced ~15 call sites with the literal decorator. The named alias expressed 'this is a kw-only frozen record' once; inlining is mechanical but not simple. Reintroduce a one-line unconditional alias so the intent is named in one place.

issues.description: PR description contradicts itself on Union/Optional ruff enforcement
issues.detail: The description says 'Union types are no longer / will soon not be supported through Ruff' with a strikethrough leaving the policy ambiguous. The diff does not appear to flip the ruff config. Either land the rule change with the description or remove the claim; ambiguous commit messages are hostile to future maintainers.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a correct and overdue removal of Python 3.9 scaffolding, with clean mechanical edits across CI, install scripts, and dataclass call sites. Two cleanup misses recur across all three reviewers: install.sh still gates on `-lt 7` while advertising `>= 3.10`, and the default_raise helper plus its '< 3.10 compatibility' comments survive despite their rationale evaporating. Torvalds additionally flags that this is really three patches (CI/install, kw_only consolidation, itertools.pairwise) bundled into one, hurting bisect. Smaller hygiene issues — dnf search noise in CI, lost named intent from inlining kw_only_dataclass, and an ambiguous PR description on ruff Union enforcement — round out the list. Verdict: needs-work, finish the cleanup the PR started.
